titulo: He hasn't got an ounce of sense
intro: Describing character precisely: the nouns for qualities, the adjectives, and a few colourful idioms.
p.hipócrita.nota: The same form for both genders.
p.no tener dos dedos de frente: to have no sense at all
b1.texto:
At B2 you talk about qualities as things, so you need the nouns.

- **-dad**: generoso → **la generosidad**; sincero → **la sinceridad**; serio → **la seriedad**; puntual → **la puntualidad**; responsable → **la responsabilidad**; sensible → **la sensibilidad**; curioso → **la curiosidad**.
- **-ez**: tímido → **la timidez**; maduro → **la madurez**.
- **-ía**: valiente → **la valentía**; cobarde → **la cobardía**; hipócrita → **la hipocresía**.
- **-ura**: tierno → **la ternura**.
- **-ismo**: egoísta → **el egoísmo**; optimista → **el optimismo**.
- **-ción / -cia**: ambicioso → **la ambición**; arrogante → **la arrogancia**; constante → **la constancia**.

The prefixes **in-**, **im-** and **ir-** make the opposite: **inconstante**, **impuntual**, **irresponsable**, **insensible**, **la insinceridad**.

**Ser or tener.** **Es** valiente = **tiene** valentía. Fixed phrases: **tener carácter** or **tener personalidad** (to be strong-minded); **tener mal carácter** (to be bad-tempered); **ser de carácter tranquilo**; **tener complejo de** inferioridad; **estar acomplejado**.

**False friend.** **Sensible** means sensitive. Sensible is **sensato**.

**Idioms.** **No tiene dos dedos de frente**: he has no sense. **Está como una cabra**: he is mad, said with affection. **Es un trozo de pan**: he is very kind. **Tiene mucha cara**: he has a nerve.
b2.f0: My two uncles are brothers, but it is hard to believe, because they are nothing alike.
b2.f1: Fermín is ambitious and persevering: he started as a waiter and today has three restaurants.
b2.f2: Mind you, he is so mean that he has never bought anyone a coffee.
b2.f3: Eusebio, on the other hand, has a calm nature and a generosity that sometimes borders on irresponsibility.
b2.f4: My grandmother used to say he had no sense at all, because he lent money to anyone who asked him for it.
b2.f5: The curious thing is that the brave one in the family was always him, and not Fermín.
b2.f6: When someone had to stand up to the owner of the premises, Fermín, with all his arrogance, kept quiet out of sheer cowardice.
b4.pregunta: According to the text, which brother is mean with money?
b4.o0.refuerzo: Es tan tacaño que nunca ha invitado a nadie.
b4.o1.refuerzo: He is generous to a fault.
b4.o2.refuerzo: Both is wrong: the question asks which single brother is mean with money.
b5.pregunta: According to the text, who was the brave one?
b5.o0.refuerzo: El valiente de la familia siempre fue él.
b5.o1.refuerzo: He kept quiet out of cowardice.
b6.pregunta: Complete with the noun of tímido.
b7.pregunta: Es una persona muy sensible means…
b9.o0.refuerzo: Before r, the prefix is ir-.
b11.traduccion: He is so mean that he never treats anyone.
b12.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write a portrait of two very different people, contrasting their characters with nouns and adjectives.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Talk aloud about which qualities you value most in a friend, a boss and a partner, and why.
b10.o0.explicacion: Tiene mucho carácter means she has a strong personality.
